A LOOK UNDER THE BONNET

Details in.

01

Names stay categories

Make and model enter LightGBM as ordinary categorical fields alongside mileage, year and other vehicle details. No transformer or separate price model is fitted to those names.

02

Descriptions get their own signal

The GPU workflow fine-tunes MiniLM-L6 on seller descriptions and log prices. Three-fold predictions create predicted_text_price without using each row’s own price to train its predictor.

TRAINING PENDING
03

Filter, then combine

Isolation Forest uses automatic contamination on training OOF text prices only. It determines the removal count; validation/test remain unfiltered. Huber LightGBM then combines the text-price signal with the structured fields.

THE MODEL TAKES THE WITNESS STAND

Explain the price.
Without the mystic fog machine.

For the curious car buyer and the person who reads loss-function documentation for fun.

In ordinary human

LightGBM is a committee of small decision trees. Each new tree corrects earlier mistakes. They have read thousands of listings; none has inspected your clutch.

What goes in?

Year, mileage, make, model and vehicle details. Make and model are categories, not neural embeddings. The active baseline does not read seller descriptions.

Why log price?

A $1,000 error means something different on a $3,000 hatchback and a $90,000 SUV. A log-price target makes relative differences more comparable. This baseline was selected using validation error in real dollars.

What is Huber?

A loss function that softens the influence of very large errors. One seller asking the price of a small castle does not get to chair the committee.

What if? A small thought experiment.

Change one feature of the last car you estimated. This reruns the actual fitted trees. It does not prove that changing a car causes that price change.

First estimate a car on Value a car.

Other inputs stay fixed. Some feature combinations are unusual or historically impossible; extrapolation is risky. This sensitivity tool is not SHAP.

Under the bonnet · technical

Prediction maths and interpretation

The deployed baseline sums leaf scores from the fitted trees. Its standardized output r is converted to z = mean + std × r, then price = exp(clip(z, 0, log(1 + 10⁷))) − 1 for log1p targets. Rounding in the main estimate is display-only.

Native TreeSHAP explanations are available in the Python / Streamlit GUI after each estimate. They satisfy z = reference + Σ feature contributions before clipping. For log targets, contributions add in log(1 + price) space and multiply price + 1 after exponentiation; they are not additive dollar discounts. The reference is not the mean dollar price.

Tree-path-dependent SHAP allocates shared credit within the fitted tree ensemble. Correlated fields can share or shift that credit. Global split gain is a training summary, not a per-car explanation, an accuracy metric, or causal evidence.

Text model, leakage and outliers

The enhanced workflow fine-tunes MiniLM-L6 on descriptions and standardized log1p(price). Three-fold out-of-fold predictions create a scalar predicted_text_price without using each predicted row’s own target in its text predictor. Make/model remain categorical.

Isolation Forest uses contamination=auto on training OOF text prices only. It removes no preset percentage. Validation and test stay unfiltered. The enhanced LightGBM is selected by validation MAE across Huber settings and raw/log targets, tested chronologically, then refitted using fresh all-row OOF features. The scalar text-price feature can be attributed by TreeSHAP; individual words cannot be explained by that LightGBM attribution.

This web interface runs the trained tabular baseline locally. It does not connect to the Kaggle job or claim enhanced results before importing its completed model.

Errors, uncertainty and the awkward bits

MAE is average absolute dollar error; RMSE punishes large misses more strongly. R² compares squared error with a constant mean-price predictor on the evaluated set. The indicative 80% band was calibrated on validation log residuals; measured test coverage appears in Model results. It is not an individual guarantee.

Assessment uses chronological 70/15/15 splits after eligibility checks and deduplication. The deployment model was refitted on every eligible baseline row, so the published assessment scores are not independent evaluation of that final refit. These are 2021 asking prices, not current transaction values. A clean title still does not mean a clean engine.
